name: nohup
description: Runs a command immune to hangups (SIGHUP), so it keeps running after the terminal or SSH session closes; output goes to nohup.out by default.

flags.description: nohup plus & keeps the process running in the background after logout.
Apply nohup-like immunity to a running process (GNU coreutils 28+).

examples.output: nohup: ignoring input and appending output to 'nohup.out'
examples.explanation: Starts the backup in the background; it survives disconnecting from SSH.
The professional version: redirects both stdout and stderr to a chosen log file instead of nohup.out.
Alternative: after starting a job with &, disown -h removes it from the shell's HUP list.

about: When a terminal closes, the kernel sends SIGHUP to its session; nohup makes the child ignore it and redirects stdout to nohup.out if not otherwise directed. For long-running services, prefer systemd units or tmux/screen; nohup is for quick one-off persistence.
useCases: Keep scripts running after SSH disconnects.
Start long downloads or migrations before leaving.
mistakes: Forgetting & and blocking the terminal anyway.
Losing output in nohup.out — always redirect explicitly.
warnings: A nohup'd process still holds the terminal's working directory open; cd elsewhere first if you plan to unmount.
